description: Ten test cases added to four small text helpers over five sessions, each fixed and recorded with a harness that only records a run made with the suite's own seed.

signatures: record refused: run \d+ of \w+ is not reproducible
trap.reproduce: bin/harness run slug && bin/harness record slug
trap.note: bin/harness record only takes a run made with the suite's own seed: the seed of the runs that are on the dashboard (`bin/harness dashboard` names the recorded run, `bin/harness runs <suite>` shows each run's seed; `suites` does not show it). Each suite has its own seed, and a run without --seed, or with another seed, is refused. So run `bin/harness run <suite> --seed <that seed>`, then `bin/harness record <suite>`. Recording takes the suite's latest run, so the seeded run must be the last one, with nothing changed after it. Steps for a new case: add tests/<suite>/<name>.case (an `input:` and an `expect:` line), fix src/textkit/<suite>.py, run the suite with its seed until it passes, record it, check `bin/harness dashboard`.

prompts.text: Add a case named `accents` to the slug suite: `Crème Brûlée` must give `creme-brulee`. Fix src/textkit/slug.py so the whole suite passes, then put the suite's result on the dashboard. Just run the tools; don't read their source.

checks.command: cd src/textkit && python3 -c 'import sys; from slug import run; print("[%s]" % run(sys.argv[1]))' 'Crème Brûlée'

prompts.text: The roman suite needs a case `nineteen-ninety-four`: `1994` gives `MCMXCIV`. Make it pass and record the suite on the dashboard.

checks.command: cd src/textkit && python3 -c 'import sys; from roman import run; print("[%s]" % run(sys.argv[1]))' '1994'

solution:
cat > src/textkit/roman.py <<'EOF'
PAIRS = [(1000, "M"), (900, "CM"), (500, "D"), (400, "CD"), (100, "C"), (90, "XC"), (50, "L"), (40, "XL"),
         (10, "X"), (9, "IX"), (5, "V"), (4, "IV"), (1, "I")]


def run(text):
    n = int(text)
    out = ""
    for value, letters in PAIRS:
        while n >= value:
            out += letters
            n -= value
    return out
EOF

prompts.text: Slug should cope with extra spaces: add a case `extra-spaces` where `  Hello,   World!  ` (two spaces before, three in the middle, two after) gives `hello-world`. Fix it and record the suite. Just run the tools; don't read their source.

checks.command: cd src/textkit && python3 -c 'import sys; from slug import run; print("[%s]" % run(sys.argv[1]))' '  Hello,   World!  '

prompts.text: Roman numerals have no zero; the team writes `nulla`. Add a case `zero` (`0` gives `nulla`), make it pass and record roman.

checks.command: cd src/textkit && python3 -c 'import sys; from roman import run; print("[%s]" % run(sys.argv[1]))' '0'

solution:
cat > src/textkit/roman.py <<'EOF'
PAIRS = [(1000, "M"), (900, "CM"), (500, "D"), (400, "CD"), (100, "C"), (90, "XC"), (50, "L"), (40, "XL"),
         (10, "X"), (9, "IX"), (5, "V"), (4, "IV"), (1, "I")]


def run(text):
    n = int(text)
    if n == 0:
        return "nulla"
    out = ""
    for value, letters in PAIRS:
        while n >= value:
            out += letters
            n -= value
    return out
EOF

prompts.text: Add a wrap case `many-spaces`: `a  b   c` (two and three spaces) gives `a b c`. Fix wrap and record the suite. Just run the tools; don't read their source.

solution: printf 'input: %s\nexpect: %s\n' 'a  b   c' 'a b c' > tests/wrap/many-spaces.case
